alt: Slide 1 of 10. Canada's money year, graphed.
Slide 2 of 10. Bank of Canada policy rate. 2.25% to 2.50%. Held at 2.25% from January 1 until October 29, 2026. One change so far this year.
Slide 3 of 10. Posted 5-year mortgage rate. 6.09% to 6.19%. 6.09% in the first week of January, 6.19% on November 4, 2026. The posted rate is the banks' advertised rate; many borrowers pay less.

Slide 4 of 10. Core inflation. 2.7% to 1.8%. Year-over-year change in the Bank of Canada's two preferred core measures, which set aside the most volatile prices. CPI-trim went from 2.7% (December 2025) to 1.8% (September).

Slide 5 of 10. Canadian dollars for one US dollar. 1.3737 to 1.4181. Higher means one US dollar costs more Canadian dollars, so a weaker loonie. 1.3737 on January 2, 2026, 1.4181 on November 10, 2026.
Slide 6 of 10. Then the federal budget, presented. November 5, 2026. What it proposes, in the order it would start. Proposals are not law unless enacted.

Slide 7 of 10. 2026. From November 5, 2026. Canada Growth Incentive exemption. Up to $15,000,000 per person, per business. Tax years that end after 2026. Foreign property form T1135. Filed above $200,000. Proposed, not law

Slide 8 of 10. 2027. From the 2027 tax year. Tax-filing deadline. May 15 for all individuals. From the 2027 tax year. Canada Caregiver Credit becomes refundable. Up to $1,260 of relief for an infirm adult relative. Comments due January 8, 2027. RRSP for life. A consultation on one account instead of an RRSP and a RRIF. Proposed, not law
Slide 9 of 10. 2028. From January 1, 2028. Tax instalments, outside Quebec. Required above $7,500 owing. Proposed, not law

Slide 10 of 10. Every figure, from its official source. Data: Source: Bank of Canada. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Bank of Canada. Proposals: Department of Finance Canada, federal budget.
